ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the parabola $y=ax^2+3ax+c$ ($a>0$) intersects the y-axis at point C and the x-axis at points A and B, with point A to the left of point B. The coordinate of point B is $(1, 0)$, and $OC=3OB$. Find the equation of the parabola.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Because the coordinates of B are $(1,0)$,\\
therefore $OB = 1$.\\
Because $OC = 3OB = 3$, and point C is below the x-axis,\\
therefore C is $(0, -3)$.\\
Because substituting B $(1,0)$, C $(0, -3)$ into the quadratic equation yields $\begin{cases}4a+c=0\\ c=-3\end{cases}$, solving gives: $\begin{cases}a=\frac{3}{4}\\ c=-3\end{cases}$,\\
therefore the equation of the parabola is $\boxed{y=\frac{3}{4}x^{2}+\frac{9}{4}x-3}$.
